# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

S5 Add ISO 8601 duration parsing (`parseISO`) to the ms library as the inverse of `formatISO`, with exports and tests (Nov 3, 2:34 AM)
**Investigated**: The `formatISO` commit bcd0d52 and its layout: the implementation sits in `src/index.ts` and its tests in `src/format-iso.test.ts`, with no separate module. The existing `parse()` regex and error handling, which `parseISO` was modeled on. The package test scripts, which run Node and edge suites.

**Learned**: `formatISO` rounds to whole milliseconds, prefixes negatives with `-`, returns `PT0S` for zero, and throws on non-finite input. A `parseISO` inverse must accept the sign prefix and produce the same rounding, so round-trips hold. `parse()` returns `NaN` for unmatched input and throws for invalid argument types, and `parseISO` follows that convention.

**Completed**: `parseISO` is exported from `src/index.ts`. It parses days, hours, minutes, and fractional seconds with an optional leading `+` or `-`, rounds to whole milliseconds, and returns `NaN` for unsupported or malformed input (years, months, weeks, empty designators). It throws for non-strings and for strings that are empty or longer than 100 characters. Tests are in `src/parse-iso.test.ts`, including a round-trip check against `formatISO`. Node and edge suites pass with 185 tests and 100% coverage, and typecheck and lint are clean. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: Waiting on confirmation to commit the `parseISO` work, with a suggested branch of `feat/iso-duration`. No commit or push has happened yet.

**Notes**: The implementation uses a regex, the same approach `parse()` takes. An earlier note mentioned a possible team rule against regex that was never verified, so that should be checked before a PR is opened. The `parse()` error message still says "between 1 and 99" while its check allows 100, an existing inconsistency that is unchanged. `parseISO`'s error message says "between 1 and 100", which matches its own check.
